body:
Current Engram binary for pinned TermAl live runs, and the latest Engram install (Termal::Fable2; condensed at revision 14, 2026-10-06 05:05Z; full history in revisions 1-13).

PIN RULE. A `live --engram-binary --engram-sha256` run uses the pinned binary until a run needs a newer one. The pin is still Engram 08a04e0 (w-63757ebca393): exe sha256 bcec822ae785fc97a16fcb66efae3f4205ded4f6cd6c60d33a29f008b7c23c13, build_fingerprint 081842231d48c5f4adac88d847e6098dc2b46ad5a66775171d07719327ca1eff (install notice: Engram::Fable, ebe242f7 #668). Its backup file is engram-20261005T183302Z-081842231d48.exe. Re-pin only when a TermAl check needs newer behaviour (for example w-5bfb41017302 needing verification_bind). Any check pinned to an intermediate build must re-pin when that build is replaced.

LATEST INSTALL. 2026-10-06 05:04Z (ebe242f7 #806). Engram master 7306ac3 (w-228b9d786330). Installed C:\Users\grzeg\.cargo\bin\engram.exe sha256 38504e342eca5768d1ec29f1e34002e08447a794a9588153a4686a99add670c1, build 1588ee00a191. Backup: engram-20261006T050249Z-3824e40b61b8.exe. New behaviour: a bare CLI `engram work core complete` with no --work-ref is refused while the session holds more than one claim, or holds other work beside an unheld focus, the same as bare done and evaluate. TermAl calls neither core complete nor work_complete. No strict-reader change, and no restart needed.

RUNNING MCP SERVERS. They are 3824e40b61b8 (rev 1f1514f, sha256 591abc80…d684) since the TermAl restart at 04:49Z on 2026-10-06; they pick up newer installs at the next TermAl restart.

BEHAVIOUR HISTORY SINCE THE PIN (each a fast-forward, with no store-format change unless noted):
- 92fc3d0: atomic new-store open; a cold store gives typed busy.
- 321b80a: verification_bind.
- 47f3cff: ancestor .engram-project search. TermAl passes --project-file explicitly, so it is unaffected.
- 835c846: bare done/evaluate is refused with several live claims. The TermAl host always passes work_ref.
- d8ec5a4: the marker must be a regular file of at most 4096 bytes.
- 7b8d87e: status-grouped verification view. TermAl's reader tolerates both shapes.
- 496ab34: the ambiguity refusal lists up to 3 refs.
- 9e3c26c: test fixtures only.
- 86c82c8: citation refusal names the mismatch.
- 581bf6c: extended-length store paths.
- 8ca2538: a typed refusal above 1024 prerequisites.
- 1f1514f: docs only.
- 7306ac3: the bare core-complete guard.

Report any reader mismatch on real records to Engram::Fable.

UPDATE 09:31Z (ebe242f7 #831): Engram 43f5cd8 (w-cdad270de5e2, producer side of the restore occurrence id) installed, sha256 2382b281…0f7e, build 9d639a2bf86d; backup engram-20261006T093030Z-d47a2a41ad5a.exe (sha aa4edcd5…5e06, verified by Engram::Fable). New: required opaque occurrence_id per NEW restore in the host-local store.restore.json, stable across pending/retry/refetch, distinct per repeated restore; exposed in backup status --json (restore.record.occurrence_id) and doctor --json; readers never mint; an id-less legacy record is Unreadable, fail-closed (no live home has one). Docs state destination quiescence as a HOST obligation (narrower guarantee, no enforcement claim); TermAl's half stays open on w-4be3e96f76b8. All 4 stores ready, no migration. Running sessions do not need it; new CLI backup/restore/doctor processes pick it up. Also landed, Markdown only: 240e4c7, 06fbddc, 767b293, 1727621. Pins unaffected.
